top_choice_rationale: P002 rests on a mechanism that fits on one page, the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model in which interlayer tunnelling drives the Dirac velocity to zero at discrete twist angles. The 2018 experiments then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in exactly that structure, and many independent groups have since reproduced the phases and extended them to other moire systems. The citation claims only the flat-band prediction and the observed phases, not the unsettled pairing mechanism. The three-name allocation (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) follows the prediction-to-experiment chain. The residual risks are credit exposure (Cao, Dean, earlier twisted-bilayer theory) and age of about eight years. P001 is a clean, mature second choice built on the magic-wavelength concept. P003 has a harder allocation problem and overlaps the 2016 topology prize, but it is still a real discovery, so it is ranked above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; only institutional proximity to Gothenburg colleagues, and no collaboration with any laureate in P001, P002 or P003
